messages:
support: FYI we have a customer escalation (acct: AcmeCorp) — p99 on /v1/chat spiked ~2x for last 30m, started ~4420012000. customer sent traces + request-id r-8f6a. They see timeouts occasionally. Marking high.
maria: pinging oncall/runtime. any quick triage? what changed in last deploy? :eyes:
kevin: I pulled the deploy list — kernel-selector service rolled out v2 heuristics at 4420011800 (commit abc1234). That changed priority logic for attention kernels. Seen a few perf anomalies in staging but not this magnitude.
infra-bot: deploy kernel-selector v2 (abc1234) -> production @4420011800 by ci/bot
anjali: I can repro locally against redwood-13b-8k with the customer's payload. p95/p99 regressions jump when sequence length > 1k and small batch sizes (1-2). Repro steps:
```
# sample repro
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-8k","input":"<~1.2k tokens>"}'
```
I see p95 ~180ms (was ~110ms) and p99 ~460ms (was ~240ms) locally with CPU+GPU timing logs.
kevin: digging into kernel selection: v2 heuristic now prefers SDPA kernel for sequences between 1024-2048 when `batch_size <= 2` because of new startup-cost estimate. SDPA implementation has lower amortized cost for long seqs but higher kernel launch overhead for small batches on our current CUDA kernel build. Looks like the cost model underestimated launch latency.
dave: quick mitigation idea: flip runtime flag to force legacy heuristic for affected model/route or add a temporary override for `batch_size <= 4` to prefer FlashAttention. Can we patch config and push a hotfix? ops-sre, can you run the config change?
ops-sre: I'll do a targeted override on the routing policy for redwood-13b-8k at traffic tier prod-1. Command I use:
```
rctl update routing --model redwood-13b-8k --policy "kernel_priority:legacy_flash" --env prod --actor ops-sre
```
Applying now.
ops-sre: done @4420012500 — override applied, commit d1f4c2. Monitoring.
anjali: after override: locally observed partial rollback. p95 down to ~140ms, p99 down to ~270ms. Not fully back to baseline but much better. Customer threads show similar improvements (they confirmed decreased tail).
maria: good. we should still fix root cause; two follow-ups: 1) change the selection cost model to include launch overhead for small batches, 2) revert/adjust compile flags if kernel build exacerbates startup. kevin, can you own?
kevin: yeah I'll run kernel microbenchmarks. I suspect the compile flags enabled more aggressive inlining/FP16 path which changed kernel launch/queueing behavior. Specifically flags added in abc1234: `-DUSE_SDPA=1 -O3 -fno-math-errno` + a newer nvcc micro-op schedule. I'll run a canary that reverts the flag and compare.
maria: can we also add a perf regression test to CI that exercises small-batch long-seq cases? add to perf-suite and gate kernel-selector merges.
kevin: putting together a perf CI test and will also run a 1% traffic canary of the reverted selector next deploy. Plan:
- revert sdpa-pref flag in kernel-selector and build kernels with conservative launch tuning
- add perf test (batch=1-2, seq=1200-2000) to nightly
- rollout canary 1% -> 10% -> 100%
anjali: also adding a telemetry counter + histogram for kernel-latency (launch + execution) per kernel variant so we can detect model-specific mismatches earlier.
dave: thanks team. support, please tell AcmeCorp we've applied a temporary routing override and are working on a permanent fix; ask them to confirm any lingering issues.
support: replied to customer w/ update and ETA for permanent fix. flagged SRE escalation. :white_check_mark:
maria: assign owners: kevin -> root cause + canary; anjali -> repro/perf tests + telemetry; ops-sre -> rollback plan + patch recipe. I'll open postmortem channel and add links.
ops-sre: created #pm-opti-kernel-4420012345 and uploaded flamegraphs + perf logs.
kevin: one more note — we should consider adding a small threshold in the selection code: prefer SDPA only when estimated amortized runtime_gain > 1.2x for the given batch size. That would avoid regressions for tiny batches.
maria: agreed. follow up tomorrow with roll and postmortem. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
